chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who had two wives, and each of them gave birth to a boy. One of his wives went and breastfed a girl from among the people. Is it permissible for his son to marry this girl? He said: 'No, because she breastfed from the milk of the old man (the father).'

key_terms.الشَّيْخ: the old man (referring to the father)

ai.seo_question: Does a wife's breastfeeding of a girl create a marriage prohibition for her husband's sons?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the principle of 'radha' (breastfeeding) creating kinship, specifically addressing the scenario where a wife breastfeeds a child for another family. It establishes that the milk of the wife is attributed to her husband, thereby making the breastfed girl a mahram to his sons, a ruling derived from the Quranic verse 'and your mothers who suckled you' (Surah An-Nisa 4:23). This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the legal efficacy of wet-nursing in establishing permanent marital prohibitions.
